newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on property plan concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on property plan concerns.

text.p: Thai stocks closed lower on Monday in moderate trade as investors sold on concerns that the government faced difficulty implementing plans to assist the Thai property sector, analysts said.
The SET Index ended down 17.61 points, or 2.10 percent, to 822.89. The SET 50 fell 1.77 points to close at 61.32. Turnover was 3.98 billion baht.
"There are worries that there will be technical and practical difficulties in their plans to help the property sector," said Tanawat Patchimkul, senior analyst at Seamico Securities.
The government last week pledged up to 70 billion baht to assist lenders struggling to contain problem loans extended to some troubled real estate developers.

Comments by Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond that the bank may review rules limiting foreign ownership in banks and finance houses sparked a sell off on the foreign board, Tanawat said. Foreign ownership of Thai banks and finance houses is currently limited to 25 percent and 40 percent resepectively. Investors also sold on fears that a planned 50 billion baht government budget cut may be insufficient to significantly cut the current account deficit, Tanawat said.
Profit taking by foreigners who bought in at below the 800 level at the start of the month is expected to see the market extend losses on Tuesday, he said.
"Now with the index dropping that is not good news and I think the Europeans may well be selling tomorrow," Tanawat said.

Bank stocks were the hardest hit, with the sector dropping 3.78 percent on the day. The nation's largest banks topped the active list. Bangkok Bank lost five baht to 185, Krung Thai Bank dropped three to 52.50, Siam Commercial shed three to 170, and Thai Farmers Bank fell seven to 122.--J.Mclean (662) 652 0642
